notes: Unfilled on purpose, blocked by network, not by absence of a service - and the lead that was supposed to open it is now disproved rather than untested. The Secretary of the State's expedited-service document lived on a host that still does not answer: on the retrieval date the local resolver returned no address at all for it or for the department portal beside it, while a public resolver answered for both with the same pair of content-delivery addresses, and pinning either of those addresses with the certificate check left intact still made no TCP connection. So the classification is unchanged and the mechanism is now recorded one level finer - this is a name that resolves elsewhere and refuses to connect here, not a name that has been retired. The statutes the state does publish reachably were read in full in an earlier pass and are not repeated: the uniform limited liability company act contains no occurrence of 'expedit' at all, and the business corporations chapter's only expedited language is about court procedure, so the fee is administrative rather than statutory and only the unreachable host states it. What is new is the other half. The state's business service site was read in a browser and it is not what it was taken for: it renders as a business-assistance portal headed 'Start a New Business Checklist' that walks a founder through a personalised checklist, and it carries no fee schedule and no expedited-service page. That is not a judgement from one page - the site publishes its own enumeration, and it was read: seventeen views, all of them search, checklist, contact or account pages, and one hundred seventy-seven knowledge articles, none of which is about filing fees or expedited handling. An enumeration the publisher wrote itself rules out the site's own publications in a way a silent page cannot, so the expectation that this host had inherited the expedited-service content is closed as wrong. Nothing is recorded rather than anything guessed.
needsReview: Every expedite field and every standard-processing field, and there is now no known readable address for any of them. The two follow-ups this record used to name are both closed: the state's business service site was read and does not carry the content, proved against the site's own enumeration rather than against one page, and the department's own host is still unreachable from this network by name, by public-resolver address and by pinned address alike. What would settle it is a route on which that host connects, or a printed fee schedule published somewhere the office also controls. Until one of those exists this state cannot be closed from here, and re-probing the dead host is not the way to find out.
